notToBeConfusedWith.name: Genever
notToBeConfusedWith.note: The Dutch malt-wine spirit gin descends from: heavier, faintly sweet and grain-forward, where gin is a neutral spirit carrying botanicals.

generalSubstitutes.note: Removes the botanicals rather than replacing them; a drink built on gin's juniper backbone loses its structure and becomes a plainer one.

forms.label: London dry
forms.sourceNote: Alcoholic beverage, distilled, all (gin, rum, vodka, whiskey) 80 proof. Public domain, and generic by design: the record covers any neutral-based spirit at that strength. 80 US proof is 40% alcohol by volume by definition, which is where the strength here comes from; the record's own measured ethanol content against its measured density works out at 39.8%, which is the cross-check. Bottles run from 37.5% upwards and a stronger one moves every figure it touches.
